title: AI Regulation and Model Releases: OpenAI and Anthropic Face New Government Scrutiny
content:
Key Points and English Translation

OpenAI’s New Model Release

  • Original: OpenAI stated in its official blog that the company "believes AI should be widely open" and is working to fully launch three models—GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra, and Luna—in the coming weeks.
  • Translation: OpenAI announced that it is committed to broad AI openness and plans to roll out GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra, and Luna fully within weeks.

Government Pre-Review Concerns

  • Original: OpenAI noted that before the official release, it had already demonstrated the models’ capabilities and release plans to the U.S. government.
  • Translation: Before the launch, OpenAI showed the models to U.S. officials and outlined its deployment strategy.
  • Original quote: "We do not believe this model of government pre-review should become a long-term norm. It prevents users, developers, businesses, cybersecurity defenders, and global partners who truly need these tools from accessing the most advanced technology in a timely manner."
  • Translation: OpenAI argues that mandatory government pre-review should not be permanent, as it delays access for essential stakeholders.

No Partner List Announced

  • Original: OpenAI has not disclosed the list of initial partners authorized to use the new models.
  • Translation: OpenAI has not released the names of first-wave partners.

Anthropic’s Response to Export Controls

  • Original: Two weeks ago, OpenAI competitor Anthropic announced it had to shut down access to its two latest AI models, Mythos 5 and Fable 5, due to export control orders from the Trump administration.
  • Translation: Anthropic was forced to restrict access to Mythos 5 and Fable 5 under U.S. export rules.
  • Original: After negotiations with Washington officials, Anthropic partially reopened Mythos 5 on Friday to "trusted partners," including over 100 companies and institutions, while Fable 5 remains restricted.
  • Translation: Following talks with U.S. officials, Anthropic granted limited access to Mythos 5 for over 100 trusted partners; Fable 5 access remains unavailable.

Regulatory Shift Under Trump

  • Original: Since President Trump signed an AI executive order earlier this month, his administration has taken a more proactive regulatory stance. The order does not impose specific rules but asks AI developers to voluntarily submit models for government evaluation before full release.
  • Translation: Trump’s AI executive order, while lacking detailed regulations, encourages voluntary pre-release government reviews for AI models.

OpenAI’s Cooperation with Government

  • Original: OpenAI said it is working with the Trump administration to build evaluation mechanisms and a repeatable process for future model releases.
  • Translation: OpenAI is collaborating with the U.S. government to establish standardized evaluation and release procedures.
  • Original: "We are taking this short-term measure because we believe it is the best way to expand open access in the coming weeks."
  • Translation: OpenAI views this temporary step as optimal for achieving wider access soon.

Model Capabilities

  • Original: OpenAI’s new models—GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra, and Luna—are named by capability tier. Sol is the company’s most powerful AI model to date, with significant improvements in programming and biology, and the strongest cybersecurity capabilities.
  • Translation: GPT-5.6 Sol is OpenAI’s most advanced model, excelling in coding, biology, and security. Terra and Luna are lower-tier models.
Summary: OpenAI is releasing three new models with partial government pre-review, while Anthropic faces similar restrictions. The Trump administration is tightening AI oversight via voluntary evaluations, prompting both companies to adapt.
